newsitem.title: USA: U.S. concerned over arrests in Armenia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. concerned over arrests in Armenia.

text.p: The United States expressed concern on Tuesday over arrests in Armenia in the wake of protests over last week's presidential election and called for an explanation from the Yerevan government.
"There have been reports that some members of the opposition have been beaten by Armenian security forces," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
"We're very concerned about those reports and we'd like to hear the Armenian government's explanation of whether or not this happened, and if it did, why it happened," he said.

Diplomats and opposition politicians in Armenia said on Monday that President Levon Ter-Petrosyan, who was declared re-elected, was using recent unrest to imprison political opponents and stifle dissent.
They said that up to 250 people had been detained since the unrest, some of whom had nothing to do with protests.
Burns called on Armenia to detail where the detained people were being held and to account for their welfare.

"We continue to urge the government of Armenia to handle all detentions and arrests in a manner consistent with international human rights standards, including full respect for due process of law," Burns told reporters.

Burns said Washington was aware of allegations of irregularities in the election, but was awaiting a report from observers of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, due in the next few days.

A Washington Post editorial Tuesday criticised the U.S. administration for a "mealy-mouthed" response to events in Armenia, a country which it said received more U.S. aid per capita than any other country except Israel.
